claim: Under the plain view doctrine, evidence is lawfully discoverable when an officer is in a place where he has a right to be, the incriminating nature of the items is immediately apparent, and—as an additional requirement imposed by North Carolina law beyond federal constitutional mandates—the discovery must be inadvertent.
initial_reasoning: State v. Tabb is the North Carolina Supreme Court decision that held the plain‑view doctrine requires the officer to be in a place where he has a right to be, the incriminating nature of the items must be immediately apparent, and, in addition to the federal standard, the discovery must be inadvertent.
